raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
The backward loader waited for dO_dV(i)'s buffer before issuing Q(i+1), delaying the next score even when the MMA used lookahead. Preload the first Q tile, then issue dO(i), Q(i+1), and dO_dV(i) in the consumer's order.

Share the Q load helper with the natural-order path, preserve the empty/final-tile guards and whole-ring drains, and document the dependency in the SDPA guide. Buffer sizes, TMA counts and launch counts are unchanged.

## Before submitting

- [x] I agree to license this contribution under LICENSE.txt.
- [x] Scoped pre-commit passed.
- [x] Reviewed the applicable AGENTS.md Hard Rules.
- [x] Category, affected-area and originator labels applied.

## Affected area

FE OSS kernels / CuTeDSL: native half backward.

## Related issues

Follow-up to #1963 (THD acquire-once), now based on its landed commit. Both the parent kernel and candidate kernel are byte-identical to the sources used for the qualification below.

## API and compatibility impact

None. No public signature, graph eligibility or selection-policy change.

## Testing

From test/python with the candidate checkout confirmed as imported:

```bash
python -m pytest -o addopts= -q --disable-warnings -x sdpa/frost/test_sdpa_bwd_d192_sm100.py sdpa/frost/test_sdpa_bwd_thd_d192_sm100.py sdpa/frost/test_sdpa_bwd_half_deterministic_sm100.py sdpa/frost/test_sdpa_bwd_thd_d256_sm100.py sdpa/frost/test_sdpa_bwd_d256_sm100.py::test_mma_order_arms_match_the_fp64_reference
```

112 passed. Four physical-origin graph replay cases passed each of memcheck and synccheck with zero errors, covering D192/D256, BF16/FP16, changed bindings and empty replay. An eight-case parent comparison passed full-gradient FP64, poisoned replay, changed dO and fresh bindings in all16arms. The local aggregate improved; two long dense controls regress slightly and are retained as an explicit tradeoff. Scoped formatting and license checks passed.

reviews.body:
**Codex bot review · model: `gpt-6-astra`**

Reviewed `0fd9fb1cc310` against base `7d7d8ae639fc`.

No actionable issue found. The loader now follows the lookahead consumer's operand order while preserving one Q load and ring advance per tile, the final-tile guard, and whole-ring drains. Independent correctness, replay and synccheck checks passed. The measured cases support a limited optimization; they do not show a uniform speedup.

Validation: 112 focused tests passed with no skips on native SM100, DSL 4.8.0 and cuDNN 9.26. Coverage includes D192/D256, dense and THD storage, deterministic execution, changed bindings and lengths, empty replay, and both MMA issue orders. Six independent parent/head cases passed FP64 gradient checks and 120 poisoned eager/replay checks. All gradient bits matched within each arm and between parent and head. Four cases covered compact and physical-origin THD bindings; two covered causal and noncausal dense D192 sequences of length 2048. Four physical-origin graph-replay cases passed Compute Sanitizer synccheck with zero reported errors, covering D192/D256 and BF16/FP16. Interleaved GPU measurements on a shared SM100 engineering device used six samples per arm and excluded compilation/setup. D192 physical-origin THD measured 94.66/88.51 microseconds for parent/head; the other packed cases were near parity. Dense noncausal measured 104.61/104.63 and causal 104.40/102.96 microseconds, with overlapping sample ranges. CPU submission samples do not establish a host-side gain. Checked Q barrier arrivals, transaction bytes, ring advancement, and THD offsets against the producer/consumer paths. Started pipeline 77157000 for the current head; both changed files match its integration tree. Latest merge, style and security Actions passed.

Limitations: The full CI pipeline is still running. Its analysis job has the known worker-grouping assertion failures outside the changed source. Native SM103 and the experimental SM107 profile were not tested independently here. Shared-device timings are spot checks, not full workload qualification. The author's reported long-dense tradeoffs remain separate from these measurements; no uniform performance gain is claimed.

Approved: no P0 or high-risk P1 found. Remaining findings stay with the owner; merge timing stays with the owner.
